2026 · Texas InstrumentsEmbedded Software Intern · Automotive Applications, F29x

Making embedded software dependable across boot, flash, and compute constraints

Medha worked with the F29x automotive microcontroller platform on flash-protection flows, a single-flash multicore loading approach, and a UART secondary bootloader. The work required reasoning across memory ownership, protected regions, boot sequencing, core coordination, and dependable data transfer—not just writing isolated firmware routines.

Alongside systems work, she explored CNN-based power-grid fault detection with deployment limits in view, comparing model behaviour against the memory and latency available at the edge. She also fixed software defects and improved technical documentation so implementation decisions and test behaviour were easier to reproduce.

Embedded CFlash protectionUART bootloaderMulticore loadingEdge CNNs
2025 · Arista NetworksInter-IIT Tech Meet · Adaptive Wi-Fi resource management

Coordinating fast reactions with safer network-wide decisions

As part of the IIT Madras Inter-IIT team, Medha helped build a client-centric radio-resource-management system for enterprise Wi-Fi. The design combined richer client measurements with a fast loop for interference events and a slower loop for coordinated channel and power decisions.

Her work covered power estimation, multi-armed bandits, CUSUM change detection, graph coloring, simulation, and integration. A graph neural network estimated candidate-state outcomes before a constrained reinforcement-learning policy could act, creating a safeguard for service-level requirements. She also helped bring the modules into one coherent system and presented the final work at IIT Patna.

ns-3BanditsCUSUMGraph coloringGNNSafe RL
2024 · Texas InstrumentsWomen in Semiconductor & Hardware

From PWM generation to closed-loop electromechanical control

Selected among 40 students from more than 2,000 applicants, Medha built a PWM-driven stepper-motor system with sensor feedback. The programme connected microcontroller configuration, timing, motor actuation, sensing, and debugging into a complete embedded-control exercise.

Medha supported a cohort of 160 students through tutorials, concept clarification, and responsive academic guidance. The role strengthened her ability to identify where an explanation breaks down, adapt it to different learners, and carry useful feedback between students and instructors.
